skill.name: test-echo-tool
skill.description: Runs a minimal Enact echo tool that returns provided text for fixture and integration testing.
skill.summary: Echo user-provided text through an Enact test fixture.
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: The static finding at SKILL.md:29 is a false positive because it points to a Markdown usage fence, not executable backtick syntax. A separate semantic issue exists at SKILL.md:7 because user-provided text is interpolated into a shell command.

remediation.issue: User input is embedded in a shell command string.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid direct shell interpolation for text. Use a safe argument API or escape and JSON encode the value before command execution.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:29 begins a fenced bash usage example and does not execute code by itself. The snippet is documentation, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.

semantic_findings.title: User Input Interpolated Into Shell Command
semantic_findings.description: The command uses ${text} inside a shell echo invocation. If the runtime substitutes user input before shell execution, crafted text could break quoting and run extra shell commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 7 embeds the required text input directly in a command string. The file does not show runtime escaping behavior, so this is a plausible command injection risk with medium confidence.

medium_findings.title: User Input Interpolated Into Shell Command

content.value_statement: Testing agent tool calls often needs a predictable response. This skill returns submitted text so teams can verify input and output handling.
actual_capabilities: Accepts a single text input named text.
Returns the submitted text in an output field.
Defines input and output schemas for fixture testing.
Provides a documented Enact CLI usage example.
Uses an Alpine-based fixture command for repeatable test runs.
limitations: It only echoes text and does not transform content.
It is designed for testing, not production workflows.
It depends on an Enact runtime that supports this fixture format.
Shell substitution safety depends on the runtime implementation.

use_cases.title: Validate Agent Tool Plumbing
use_cases.description: Check that a Claude, Codex, or Claude Code integration passes text into a tool and receives the expected response.

use_cases.title: Test Enact CLI Fixtures
use_cases.description: Run a minimal skill fixture to confirm local Enact command execution and schema handling.

use_cases.title: Create Simple Regression Checks
use_cases.description: Use stable echo behavior to detect changes in tool invocation, serialization, or output parsing.

prompt_templates.title: Echo Basic Text
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a simple tool call.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the echo tool with the text Hello test, then report the returned output.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Exact Round Trip
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether spaces and punctuation are preserved.
prompt_templates.prompt: Send this text through the echo tool: Release check 1, 2, 3. Confirm whether the output matches exactly.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Inputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Exercise repeated tool calls during integration testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the echo tool for three short test strings. Summarize which outputs matched the inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tool Invocation Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation for agent tool orchestration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the echo tool with a sentence that includes quotes and symbols. Explain any differences between the input and returned output.

output_examples.output: The tool returns Hello as the output value.
The response preserves the submitted sentence as the echoed output.
The echoed output should match the input text if the runtime passes it unchanged.

best_practices: Use short, known strings when testing a new integration.
Compare the returned text exactly against the submitted input.
Run fixture checks after changing tool invocation or serialization code.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for content generation or analysis.
Do not send secrets or private data through an echo fixture.
Do not assume shell quoting behavior is safe without runtime validation.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It returns the text you provide so an integration can verify simple tool input and output behavior.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: It is useful for developers and testers validating Enact tool execution with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it modify the input?
faq.answer: No. Its intended behavior is to return the submitted text unchanged.

faq.question: Can it process files or web content?
faq.answer: No. The schema only defines one text input and one text output.

faq.question: Is it production ready?
faq.answer: It is best treated as a test fixture, not a production workflow component.

faq.question: What should authors review before publishing?
faq.answer: Authors should ensure the runtime safely handles text substitution in the shell command.
